open_points.subject: R0-04 vs R0-26 — context answer
open_points.text: the fields stay, but every read is authenticated and carries the disclosure class of what it returns
open_points.question: The `context` answer carries `address` (now `personal_data`, R0-38) and the customer, and PresuPro and Client Portal pin it field for field. R0-26 forbids mixing classes in one answer. What does `context` return to a caller whose token does not allow `personal_data`, Cabinet Kernel for the agent included?
options: refuse the whole call
omit or blank `address`, which breaks field-for-field
a separate projection operation without `address`, with `context` kept for personal_data-cleared tokens only
open_points.default_guess: keep `context` unchanged for tokens cleared for personal_data and add a separate non-personal projection for the others

open_points.subject: read a project / list projects
open_points.text: the project card (any status, V1-7) with its object and rooms … in its disclosure class
open_points.question: The card contains the object's address and characteristics, which are `personal_data`. What do the card and list items contain for a caller below that class: are fields dropped, is the call refused, or is there a separate projection? And what class do `customer_ref` and the project name carry?
options: fields above the caller's class are omitted
refuse the call
a dedicated lower-class projection
open_points.default_guess: a dedicated lower-class projection without object personal fields; customer_ref and name as business_confidential

open_points.subject: R0-38 vs create a project
open_points.text: A project has exactly one object
open_points.question: 'create a project' no longer requires an address and takes no object, and the object has its own 'record' action. Can a project exist without an object between creation and recording? Is the object required at creation, and can a service (Kernel) create a project with an address it supplies?
options: object optional until recorded
object required in the create request
an empty object created with every project
open_points.default_guess: object optional until recorded; 'exactly one' means at most one, recorded by the owner

open_points.subject: correct a project vs record or correct a project's object
open_points.text: the project with the new name, customer or object, next revision
open_points.question: Is the object corrected through 'correct a project' or only through its own action? When the object changes, which revision moves (the project's, the object's or both), and against which revision is staleness checked?
options: object only via its own action, own revision
via either, with both revisions moving
open_points.default_guess: object only via its own action; correcting a project changes name and customer only

open_points.subject: create a project / add a room / list projects by Cabinet Kernel
open_points.text: Operations with agent authority on a project are confined to the project of the current context
open_points.question: Kernel's token carries agent authority, which is confined to the working context. Can Kernel create a new project, which is outside any context? Is 'add a room' limited to the context project? Does 'list projects' or 'validate' with agent authority show projects other than the context project?
options: create allowed and not confined; other reads confined
create not allowed under agent authority
lists not confined
open_points.default_guess: under agent authority, create is not allowed and reads and room adds are confined to the context project

open_points.subject: R0-07 vs R0-34 — caller-supplied id in production
open_points.text: an id crosses into production only by an explicit import
open_points.question: Can an ordinary 'create a project' in production still accept a caller-supplied `project_id`, or does production only mint ids, with supplied ids allowed only through import?
options: production create accepts supplied ids
production create mints only; supplied ids only by import
open_points.default_guess: supplied ids still accepted by create, used for idempotent retry; foreign ids enter only by import

open_points.subject: import a project with its identity
open_points.text: the project under the identity it carries in its source
open_points.question: What is the import's source: another instance's API, an export file, or the legacy store? How do imported ids keep their source identity when R0-34 gives test instances an identity space separate from production's? And how does migrating customer contact data square with 'no production personal data' in test instances?
options: export file from the legacy VPS/local stores
pull from another instance
imports from test instances re-minted, only legacy ids kept
open_points.default_guess: an export file of the legacy instances; legacy ids are kept; projects from test instances are never imported

open_points.subject: R0-40 vs R0-03/R0-06 and archive
open_points.text: archived projects: five years after the project is closed (archived) … erased or anonymised
open_points.question: R0-06 calls customer erasure 'the only' exception to R0-03, and archiving promises 'nothing is deleted'. Is retention erasure or anonymisation of archived projects and objects a second exception? What stays readable by id afterwards, and what do consumers holding that id see?
options: second explicit exception; the id answers as anonymised
anonymise only; nothing deleted
open_points.default_guess: a second explicit exception; anonymise and keep the id readable

open_points.subject: object subject rights
open_points.text: the object's address and identifying characteristics are `personal_data`
open_points.question: The object's address is personal data, but 'Subject rights' and the actions table cover erasing and restricting only a customer's contact data. Is there an action to erase or restrict an object's address before retention ends?
options: add erase/restrict object actions
object personal data is erased only by retention
open_points.default_guess: erased only by retention; correction via 'record or correct a project's object'

open_points.subject: restrict processing of a customer
open_points.question: Can a restriction be lifted? Can a restricted customer be corrected, or newly named by a project? What does a service cleared for personal_data receive for a restricted customer?
options: add 'lift restriction'
restriction is final until erasure
open_points.default_guess: add an owner 'lift restriction' action; correction allowed; services get the customer as restricted with no contact data

open_points.subject: request a project switch
open_points.text: a pending request the owner sees in the owner interface
open_points.question: What action does the owner take on a pending request: confirm, decline, or just choose a project? Can several requests be pending at once? What happens to a request once handled or after the context changes?
options: confirm/decline actions on the request
the owner's 'choose the working project' implicitly resolves it
open_points.default_guess: explicit confirm (which performs 'choose') and decline; a newer request replaces an older one

open_points.subject: working context cardinality and reference
open_points.text: an opaque reference to the project
open_points.question: Is there one working context for the owner, or one per agent or Kernel session? And if the reference is opaque, how does the agent name the project in operations, given R0-32 speaks of the agent 'naming another project_id'? Does the agent ever receive the `project_id`?
options: one global context; agent receives project_id as business_confidential
per-agent context; only opaque reference given
open_points.default_guess: one global context for the owner; Kernel receives the project_id alongside the opaque reference

open_points.subject: location of PresuPro, Cabinet and Cabinet Kernel
open_points.text: the service API for services, reachable only on the production host and over the protected channel
open_points.question: Where do PresuPro, Cabinet and Cabinet Kernel run, and how do they reach the service API? R0-39's tunnel carries only Portal's traffic from the VPS, and no agent runs on the home server, yet Kernel runs the agent's flows.
options: all run on the home server
they run on the VPS and use the same WireGuard tunnel
Kernel runs elsewhere over its own channel
open_points.default_guess: PresuPro and Cabinet Kernel use the same home-initiated WireGuard tunnel from the VPS

open_points.subject: R0-29 owner interface coverage
open_points.text: the customer, audit and switch-request views the primary actions need
open_points.question: The owner signs in only to the owner interface, but its listed views omit several owner actions: add a room, publish and withdraw an artifact pointer, import, and restrict or erase a customer. Do these get interface views, or does the owner reach them another way?
options: all owner actions have interface views
some are administrative scripts outside the interface
open_points.default_guess: every owner action in the table has an interface view; import is a dedicated view

open_points.subject: R0-37 audit scope
open_points.text: Every significant operation leaves an audit entry
open_points.question: Which operations are significant? All writes only, or also reads of personal_data, working-context reads by Kernel, refused requests and sign-ins?
options: writes only
writes + personal_data reads + context changes + auth failures
open_points.default_guess: all writes, owner reads of personal_data, context choices and switch requests, and refused authentications

open_points.subject: onboard_object
open_points.text: a client of the API like any consumer … its staff-credential use ends with R0-30
open_points.question: Every request needs a credential, and the owner credential is held by no tool. Does onboard_object get its own service token, or is it retired?
options: retired
receives its own service token with listed operations
open_points.default_guess: retired; its role is taken by the owner interface and Kernel

open_points.subject: stale 'staff' and 'frontend' in R0-13, R0-14, R0-16
open_points.text: or staff, may withdraw it / staff find an existing one / The Registry frontend and `onboard_object` follow the new shapes
open_points.question: R0-13, R0-14 and R0-16 still name staff and the retired frontend, and carry no narrowing note. Should they read 'the owner', with the frontend reference withdrawn?
options: add narrowing notes naming R0-29/R0-30
open_points.default_guess: read 'staff' as the owner; drop the frontend from R0-13
